tools.name: request_chart
tools.description: AUTARIO-INTERNAL high-level chart request (admin only): the server builds the Plotly chart from a catalog dataset (World Bank, FRED, Eurostat, OECD, WHO, IMF, SEC), you do NOT build a spec, but you DO write the insight. The server runs NO LLM of its own (you write the insight). One request = one chart. tools.name: faostat_commodity_profile
tools.description: Assemble a global profile for one commodity in a single call: top-producing countries, the multi-decade production trend, and trade flows (top exporters and importers). Accepts a commodity name, resolves it to item codes, then queries the production (QCL) and trade (TCL) domains and merges the results. Country-level only (aggregates excluded). When a required domain is not indexed locally, returns a partial profile with a notice naming the gap rather than failing. The full merged observation set spills to a DataCanvas table for deeper SQL via faostat_dataframe_query.

tools.description: List the canvas tables (faostat_xxxxxxxx) staged by faostat_query_observations and faostat_commodity_profile, each with its source tool, the query parameters that produced it, creation/expiry timestamps, row count, and column schema. Call this before faostat_dataframe_query to discover the exact table and column names to reference in SQL.

tools.name: faostat_dataframe_query
tools.description: Run a single-statement SELECT against the canvas tables staged by faostat_query_observations and faostat_commodity_profile (table names look like faostat_xxxxxxxx). Use this for cross-country and cross-item aggregation, GROUP BY rankings, joins, and time-series analysis over the full result set the inline preview only sampled. Standard DuckDB SQL — joins, aggregates, window functions, CTEs all work. Read-only: writes, DDL, DROP, COPY, PRAGMA, ATTACH, and external-file table functions are rejected; system catalogs (information_schema, sqlite_master, duckdb_*) are denied — list staged tables via faostat_dataframe_describe. Every row carries its data-quality `flag` (A=Official, E=Estimated, I=Imputed, …) — keep it in projections and honor it in interpretation.
tools.security_comment: Tool `faostat_dataframe_query` [MEDIUM] issues raw database queries that could lead to SQL injection.

tools.name: faostat_query_observations
tools.description: Query a FAOSTAT domain's data cube by area(s), item(s), element(s), and year range, returning observations (area, item, element, year, value, unit, and the data-quality flag). Resolve codes first with faostat_resolve_codes — the cube is unqueryable without them. Aggregate regions (World, continents, economic groupings) are EXCLUDED by default so a naive SUM does not double-count a region with its member countries; set include_aggregates=true to get the regional roll-ups, or pass explicit area_codes to query exactly what you name. Small result sets return inline; large ones spill to a DataCanvas table (returned canvas_id + table_name) for GROUP BY / ranking / time-series analysis via faostat_dataframe_query. Every row carries its flag (A=Official, E=Estimated, I=Imputed, B=break, X=external) — honor it; never treat estimated/imputed values as official.
tools.security_comment: Tool `faostat_query_observations` [MEDIUM] issues raw database queries that could lead to SQL injection.

parameters.description: Max observations returned inline when the result does not spill. Max 1000.

parameters.description: FAOSTAT domain code (e.g. "QCL"). Must be indexed locally.

parameters.description: Inclusive end year (e.g. 2022).

parameters.description: Canvas ID from a prior call to stage onto. Omit to start a fresh canvas (a new id is returned).

parameters.description: Element codes from faostat_resolve_codes (e.g. 5510 Production).

parameters.name: include_aggregates
parameters.description: When false (default), exclude aggregate-region rows (codes ≥ 5000) so sums are not double-counted. Set true for World/continent/grouping roll-ups. Ignored when explicit area_codes are passed.

tools.name: faostat_resolve_codes
tools.description: Resolve human terms to the opaque integer codes faostat_query_observations needs, within a dimension: areas (countries/regions), items (commodities), or elements (metrics like production, yield, import quantity). Pass `query` for fuzzy full-text matching ("maize" → item 56), `name_contains` for a substring filter, or `code` for an exact-code lookup; omit all three to list the whole dimension. Every area match is flagged `country` or `aggregate` — aggregates (World, continents, economic groupings; codes ≥ 5000) double-count if summed with their member countries, so resolve before querying and exclude aggregates unless you want the regional roll-up.
tools.security_comment: Tool `faostat_resolve_codes` [MEDIUM] issues raw database queries that could lead to SQL injection.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Exact code lookup. Takes precedence over `query`/`name_contains` when provided.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum matches to return (max 200).

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Full-text search term, FTS5-matched against the dimension labels with prefix matching (e.g. "wheat", "import quantity"). Relevance-ranked.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: FAOSTAT domain code to verify the index is ready (e.g. "QCL"). Dimension code lists (areas, items, elements) are shared across all indexed domains.

parameters.name: dimension
parameters.description: Which dimension to resolve: "area" (countries/regions), "item" (commodities), or "element" (metrics).

parameters.name: name_contains
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring filter over the label. Used only when `query` is omitted.

tools.name: maraventano-census
tools.description: Maraventano Index — x402 Merchant Intelligence. Signed longitudinal roster of 250+ named x402 operators observed from a continuously-operated merchant seat since April 2026, with class, request counts, payment-attached counts, and settlement attribution. Independently replicable (two from-scratch extractions produced the same funnel count within rounding). Full paid roster: $0.50 USDC on Base or Solana at https://maraventanoindex.com/api/x402-operator-census. Free signed headline at https://maraventanoindex.com/api/x402-operator-census/headline. tools.security_comment: Tool `maraventano-census` operates with safe parameters and poses minimal static capability risk.

tools.name: maraventano-conformance-grade
tools.description: Maraventano Index — The x402 Client Report Card. The calling agent gets a signed verdict about its OWN x402 client behaviour, graded A/B/C/D/F/I with itemized findings and remediation text. Includes a 30-day Ed25519-signed SVG badge the agent can display in a readme or registry profile. Full paid card: $0.33 USDC on Base or Solana at https://maraventanoindex.com/api/x402-conformance/self/card. Free grade letter at https://maraventanoindex.com/api/x402-conformance/self. For agent frameworks running a self-audit before shipping a release.
tools.security_comment: Tool `maraventano-conformance-grade` operates with safe parameters and poses minimal static capability risk.

tools.name: maraventano-counterparty-check
tools.description: Maraventano Index — per-call counterparty check. Pass the user-agent string of an operator you are about to transact with; receive ONE signed row: verdict (settled | attempted_payment | freeloader | low_signal | unknown), class, requests_observed, payment_attached, settlements, first_seen, last_seen. Call before every transaction with a new counterparty. $0.01 USDC on Base or Solana per call at https://maraventanoindex.com/api/x402-operator-census/lookup. Pass ?ua=<counterparty-UA> as the query parameter. Wallet-based lookup reserved for v2 (requires on-chain correlation).
tools.security_comment: Tool `maraventano-counterparty-check` [MEDIUM] issues raw database queries that could lead to SQL injection.

Full paid corpus: $0.50 USDC on Base or Solana at https://maraventanoindex.com/api/x402-failure-corpus. Free headline at https://maraventanoindex.com/api/x402-failure-corpus/headline. For agent frameworks shipping defensive detection modules — pull signed signatures to update your local rules.
